title: The Merchant Who Lost His Memory (HI)
summary: A dishonest merchant claims he forgot borrowing five hundred gold coins due to a medical condition. Birbal restores his 'memory' with an unexpected debt.
full_text:
A wealthy trader named Seth Goverdhan borrowed five hundred gold mohurs from an elderly scholar named Shastriji to finance a spice caravan to Surat. The transaction was made verbally on mutual trust.

A year later, the spice caravan returned with vast profits. When the poor scholar visited Goverdhan's shop to ask for his five hundred coins, the merchant stared blankly and sighed:

'Alas, Shastriji! Six months ago, I was thrown from a horse and suffered a severe blow to the head! Since that tragic day, I have completely lost my memory! I do not remember borrowing a single coin from you! The physician says my memory can never return! Please leave, for you pain my infirmity!'

Weeping, Shastriji brought his grievance to Emperor Akbar.

Akbar summoned Goverdhan, who put on a convincing display of amnesia, staring with glassy eyes and repeating: 'I remember nothing! I know neither numbers nor loans!'

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can medical amnesia be cured by justice?'

Birbal smiled: 'Certainly, Your Majesty. I have an infallible psychological remedy for lost memories.'

Birbal addressed the court: 'Goverdhan's amnesia is indeed tragic. However, we have an urgent state matter.

'Three weeks ago, an imperial auditor inspecting the provincial customs registers discovered that Goverdhan's firm owes the imperial crown a back tax penalty of two thousand gold mohurs!

'Because Goverdhan has lost his memory and can no longer manage finances, the imperial treasury shall seize his warehouses, mansion, and spice stores today to satisfy the two-thousand-gold debt!'

Goverdhan's glassy eyes instantly widened with sheer terror! He leaped to his feet, waving his arms:

'Wait! Halt! It is coming back to me! My memory has returned! A miracle from heaven!'

Birbal asked calmly: 'What has returned to you, Goverdhan?'

Goverdhan cried frantically: 'I remember everything! I remember that my firm paid all imperial taxes three years ago! And I suddenly remember that I borrowed exactly five hundred gold mohurs from Shastriji for my Surat caravan!'

The entire court erupted in roaring laughter.

Birbal smiled with razor sharpness: 'Behold, Your Majesty! The mention of a two-thousand-gold penalty has instantly cured a medical condition that baffled all the physicians of Agra!'

Akbar ordered the five hundred gold coins paid to Shastriji immediately, along with an additional two hundred coins penalty for feigning illness, praising Birbal's swift cure for convenient memories.
